proof.criterion: The new documentation of a killed step says what a killed step really leaves behind
proof.surface: packages/envoy/loadtest/README.md and cluster.sh's header comment, read against what I measured in round 4
proof.observed: The section says a killed step leaves its runner job going (`loadgen run`, job `step-<name>` or `replay-<name>`, and with --typing `browsertype` as `typing-<name>`) until it ends by itself after the window, grace and drain, that it keeps loading the copy meanwhile so a step started before then measures both, that the daemons stop on their own and the jobs do not, and that `down` ends them with the runner pod. That is exactly what I measured in round 4 and reported as missing from the implementer's record: the step killed at 17:59:37 left its job running to 18:03:29, where its own log ends `step killed done: events offered 951 committed 144 …`. The remedy it gives is real in the code, not only in prose: cluster.sh:1397-1398 writes each job's pid to /work/logs/<name>.pid and its status to <name>.rc, which are the files the README's two kubectl exec lines and its `a job whose .rc file exists has ended` depend on
proof.negativeControl: I did not take the prose on trust: the pid and rc files it names are written at cluster.sh:1397-1398, and a README naming files the code did not write would have shown there as a missing grep hit
